I'm a bit late to the party. Ah well. You're onto a real thing, it's a sense of emptiness that has niggled away on my insides for the better part of a decade now. What important things are there left to do?

Do we try and scratch a living? We are so comfortable, this isn't necessary, and even if we don't consciously realize this our brains know that it's true. We don't need to scratch to survive. There is no real struggle in living. The struggle is such a fundamental part of our DNA, and it's essentially useless now. We can take that yearning to strive, the need to fight, and place that energy into a more abstract goal such as securing political freedoms, but those fights are yet another set of battles that our ancestors have essentially won for us. The only thing we can strive for is to find a slightly more attractive and compatible partner, or to send our kids to that slightly better school down the road. Big deal, right? That's really going to fulfill our primeval needs.

Basically what I'm saying is what you're feeling is exactly this primeval urge to struggle. But if society keeps filling in our basic needs, and we get further and further down the hierarchy of needs before actual effort is required, well, people are just going to live their lives wasting time on games and god damned message boards.. myself included.
